title: PhD Positions on Silicon-Carbide Quantum Networks at TU Delft, Netherlands

organization.about: TU Delft is a public technical university in Delft, the Netherlands. It offers undergraduate, master's and doctoral education across engineering, architecture, design and applied sciences. Its research connects technical knowledge with practical challenges, including energy, mobility, infrastructure and sustainability, through collaboration with industry, public organisations and international academic institutions worldwide.

intro: Fully funded TU Delft PhD positions in the Taminiau Lab (QuTech) on quantum networks based on spin defects in silicon carbide. EUR 3,204 to 4,051 gross/month. Deadline: 15 December 2026. Applicants can apply without IELTS - selection is based on documents and an English interview, not a test certificate.
description:
About the Position

TU Delft is recruiting several PhD candidates to join the Taminiau Lab at QuTech for research on quantum networks based on spin defects in silicon carbide (SiC). The project develops SiC devices that enable fast optical entanglement links and high-fidelity spin-qubit control, combining the design and fabrication of nano-photonic SiC devices with quantum optics experiments.

The goal is to demonstrate small but scalable quantum networks for distributed quantum computation, simulations and communication. The Taminiau Lab is an international and collaborative group where people from different backgrounds work closely together, share ideas openly and support each other's development.

Research Areas

  • Spin defects in silicon carbide for quantum networking
  • Design and fabrication of nano-photonic SiC devices
  • Quantum optics experiments for optical entanglement links
  • High-fidelity spin-qubit control for scalable quantum networks

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPaid doctoral employee (full-time, 38 hours/week)
SalaryEUR 3,204 to EUR 4,051 gross per month, increasing from the first to the fourth year, based on the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO).
Additional pay8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% end-of-year bonus.
DurationFour years in principle, split into two contracts: an initial 18-month contract with a go/no-go assessment, followed by 30 months after a satisfactory assessment.
TrainingEnrolment in the TU Delft Graduate School, including the Doctoral Education Programme with supervision and mentoring.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationMSc in (applied) physics, quantum technologies, material science, or a related field.
MotivationHighly motivated to work on the nano-fabrication and characterisation of quantum devices for quantum networks.
Useful experienceDevice fabrication, nanophotonics and/or experimental quantum physics (for example spins or superconducting systems) are appreciated but not essential.
EnglishEnglish proficiency is required for Doctoral Education courses and scientific writing; see TU Delft's admission policy for accepted evidence.

Application dates

Recruitment information
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when checked on 22 October 2026
Deadline15 December 2026
Start dateNot specified
LocationDelft, Netherlands

How to Apply

Apply online through the official vacancy page using the application button. Applications sent by email or post are not processed. Prepare a CV and a motivation letter; check the advert for any additional documents such as transcripts or references.

About TU Delft and QuTech

TU Delft is a technical university in Delft, the Netherlands. The position is hosted in the Taminiau Lab at QuTech, the institute for quantum technology shared by TU Delft and the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO), whose mission is to develop scalable prototypes of a quantum computer and a quantum internet.

Official Link

  • Official advert and application (verified link)
  • All current vacancies at TU Delft (official careers portal)

English language requirements

No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is requested for this employed Dutch position; English is assessed through the application documents and an interview in English.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 15 December 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
